LFU Cache — Implement from Scratch

Least Frequently Used — evicts the item with the lowest access count. Tie-break: if two items have the same frequency, evict the least recently used one (LRU within same freq bucket). Uses 3 HashMaps + LinkedHashSet for O(1) everything. LeetCode #460.
Hard LeetCode #460 Amazon · Google · Meta
get() O(1) put() O(1) Space O(capacity)

Core Idea

What is LFU?

A fixed-capacity cache that evicts the key with the lowest frequency (access count). If multiple keys share the minimum frequency, the oldest one (LRU) among them is evicted.

Every get() and put(update) increments that key's frequency.

LRU vs LFU

LRULFU
EvictsOldest accessLeast accessed
BiasRecencyFrequency
Structure1 HashMap + 1 DLL3 HashMaps
DifficultyMediumHard
2

Three-Map Architecture

keyToValue
Map<K, V>
value lookup
keyToFreq
Map<K, int>
frequency tracker
freqToKeys
Map<int, LinkedHashSet>
freq → ordered keys
LinkedHashSet maintains insertion order, so the first element is the oldest (LRU tie-break). iterator().next() gives the eviction candidate in O(1).
minFreq — an integer tracking the current minimum frequency. Avoids scanning all frequency buckets on eviction. Updated on increaseFreq() and reset to 1 on every new insertion.
3

Operations

get(key)

  1. Look up in keyToValue → O(1)
  2. Call increaseFreq(key)
  3. Return value

put(key, value)

  1. If exists → update value + increaseFreq
  2. If full → evict from freqToKeys[minFreq]
  3. Add to all 3 maps, freq=1
  4. Set minFreq = 1

increaseFreq(key)

  1. Get current freq, compute newFreq = freq + 1
  2. Remove key from freqToKeys[freq]
  3. If that set is now empty AND freq == minFreq → minFreq++
  4. Add key to freqToKeys[newFreq]
  5. Update keyToFreq

Fields & Constructor

private final int capacity;
private int minFreq;

private final Map<Integer, Integer> keyToValue;         // key → value
private final Map<Integer, Integer> keyToFreq;          // key → current frequency
private final Map<Integer, LinkedHashSet<Integer>> freqToKeys;  // freq → ordered keys (LRU)

public LFUCache(int capacity) {
    this.capacity = capacity;
    this.minFreq = 0;
    this.keyToValue = new HashMap<>();
    this.keyToFreq = new HashMap<>();
    this.freqToKeys = new HashMap<>();
}
2

get(key)

O(1)
public int get(int key) {
    if (!keyToValue.containsKey(key)) return -1;
    increaseFreq(key);
    return keyToValue.get(key);
}
3

put(key, value)

O(1)
public void put(int key, int value) {
    if (capacity == 0) return;

    // Case 1: Key exists → update value + increase frequency
    if (keyToValue.containsKey(key)) {
        keyToValue.put(key, value);
        increaseFreq(key);
        return;
    }

    // Case 2: Cache is full → evict the LFU key
    if (keyToValue.size() == capacity) {
        evict();
    }

    // Case 3: Add new key with freq=1
    keyToValue.put(key, value);
    keyToFreq.put(key, 1);
    freqToKeys.computeIfAbsent(1, k -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).add(key);
    minFreq = 1;  // new key always has freq=1
}
4

increaseFreq — the key helper

O(1)
private void increaseFreq(int key) {
    int freq = keyToFreq.get(key);
    int newFreq = freq + 1;

    keyToFreq.put(key, newFreq);

    // Remove from old frequency bucket
    LinkedHashSet<Integer> oldSet = freqToKeys.get(freq);
    oldSet.remove(key);

    // If old bucket is empty AND it was the minFreq → bump minFreq
    if (oldSet.isEmpty()) {
        freqToKeys.remove(freq);
        if (freq == minFreq) {
            minFreq++;
        }
    }

    // Add to new frequency bucket
    freqToKeys.computeIfAbsent(newFreq, k -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).add(key);
}
5

evict — remove LFU (+ LRU tie-break)

O(1)
private void evict() {
    LinkedHashSet<Integer> minFreqKeys = freqToKeys.get(minFreq);

    // First element of LinkedHashSet = OLDEST (LRU tie-break)
    int evictKey = minFreqKeys.iterator().next();

    minFreqKeys.remove(evictKey);
    if (minFreqKeys.isEmpty()) {
        freqToKeys.remove(minFreq);
    }
    keyToValue.remove(evictKey);
    keyToFreq.remove(evictKey);
}

Common Follow-ups

Why LinkedHashSet and not ArrayList?

LinkedHashSet gives O(1) remove(key) + O(1) iterator().next() + maintains insertion order. An ArrayList would make removal O(n). A plain HashSet doesn't maintain insertion order for LRU tie-breaking.

Why does minFreq++ work?

When the old freq bucket becomes empty and freq == minFreq, the key that was just accessed moved to freq+1. Since no other key can have a frequency between freq and freq+1, incrementing is always correct.

LFU with aging / decay?

Pure LFU has a "frequency stagnation" problem — old popular items stay forever. Fix: halve all frequencies periodically ("aging") or use a time-weighted frequency like freq * decay^(now - lastAccess).

When is LFU better than LRU?

LFU works better for workloads with stable popularity (CDN, DNS). LRU is better for temporal locality (recent items likely accessed again). Most real systems use LRU because it's simpler and handles bursty workloads better. Redis supports both.

3

Edge Cases & Gotchas

capacity == 0 — Must handle as a special case. Every put() is a no-op. Easy to forget and get a division-by-zero or NPE on the freq bucket.
minFreq reset on insert — After adding a new key, minFreq must be set to 1, not left at its old value. The new key has freq=1, which is always the new minimum.
computeIfAbsent — Use freqToKeys.computeIfAbsent(freq, k -> new LinkedHashSet<>()) to avoid null checks when creating a new frequency bucket.
